kitDescription: Elegg: Boom and Shock is a Water machine-gun Attacker (Burst III) who banks a counter of captured ghosts over the fight — the team's cumulative hits feed captures on a 6-second recurring cycle, up to a maximum of 13 ghosts. The ghost count is a dial on her team buff for Water allies: at one or more ghosts every Water ally gains flat ATK worth 16.2% of Elegg's own ATK, and at four or more they additionally gain 35% Elemental Advantage Attack Damage, both held for as long as the count stays there. Her burst spends ghosts as ammunition: below 13 she fires six sequential 800% hits and spends 6 (never dropping below one ghost), and at a full 13 she instead fires thirteen 800% hits and spends 9. Casting burst also gives her +40% ATK for 10 seconds. If a ghost is captured while she is already at the 13 cap, that overflow detonates for 1100% of her final ATK on all enemies. In practice she is a slow-ramping Water-team amplifier whose whole damage profile depends on how fast the entire team's fire accrues ghosts versus how often she spends them.

redAssertions: S2b describe → it('actually fires in a 180s fight (the at-cap condition is reachable) and is elegg-only') — asserts NO_NUKE[SLUG] < BASE_T[SLUG]; under the driver's interval:6 accrual the pool peaks ~7 while bursting on cooldown, so the 1100% block fires 0× in the standard control comp and zeroing it moves nothing. Classified RECON_ERROR: the assertion encodes the S5 author's own ⚑-flagged, unverified premise that accrual outruns the burst spend, and it contradicts the S2b spec, which explicitly demanded the TWO-SIDED treatment (zero events in the standard rotation + an engineered pool==13 / suppressed-burst scenario proving reachability) that the driver's H3 and H5 implement. All other 22 S5 assertions are GREEN against the shipped override; the 3 skips are the S5 author's own ⚑ GAPs (accrual cadence, min-1 floor, possession target).

(2) OFF-BY-ONE: the min:13 gate can fire on the capture that takes the pool 12→13, which the wording ('captured WHILE AT maximum capacity') does not grant. Reachability is proven two-sidedly (zero while bursting; the disableBursts run) exactly as the S2b spec demanded, and the ungated-nuke counterfactual discriminates the gate.

The −6 spend is ordered AFTER the damage effects, so the gate reads the pre-spend pool; the ≠13 block preceding the =13 block prevents the double-pay the S6 blind warned about, and the engineered-13 run confirms 13 hits (not 19) on the first cast.

gotchas.summary: 'Continuously' is encoded as a POLLED 6-second buff, so the ≥4 Elemental-Advantage aura lingers up to ~6s after a burst spend drops the pool below 4 — and that stale window lands inside Full Burst, the highest-multiplier part of the fight.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: both S1 tiers say 'continuously' (live exactly while the ghost gate holds). Driver: teamAmmo:100 trigger + resourceGate + durationSec:6 + maxStacks:1, because a `passive` block evaluates its resourceGate once at frame 0 (driver cites sim.ts:2169) and never re-reads it. The ≠13 burst spends −6 from a pool of ~7 → 1, so the ≥4 gate closes AT THE CAST — but the already-applied 35% runs out its remaining duration, and per SSOT §7 the B3 cast is only 22f before the FB countdown, so the leftover sits inside the 10s Full Burst window (Major +0.5). Blind S6 hit the identical engine wall and chose interval:1 / durationSec:2 — a ≤2s stale window vs the driver's ≤6s — so the blind independently corroborates both the problem and a tighter fix.
gotchas.suggestedFix: No magnitude change. Either (a) shorten durationSec on the two teamAmmo pool-check blocks to the smallest value that still bridges consecutive checks — measure the worst-case inter-check gap in the fixture (team ammo consumption stalls during Elegg's 171f reload and helm's charge, so it is NOT uniformly ~1s) and set the duration just above it; the generator beam-search argument does not apply here because these blocks are teamAmmo-triggered, not `interval`; or (b) the faithful representation — add the engine primitive: re-evaluate a passive block's resourceGate per frame (a resource-gated aura), which makes 'continuously' mean exactly while-gated with no lead or lag.

gotchas.summary: The 1100% at-cap nuke fires on every teamAmmo:100 pool-check while the pool holds 13, not once per capture — roughly a 6× over-fire wherever the block is reachable at all.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Activates when a ghost is captured while at maximum ghost capacity' — one event per capture, which under the driver's own accrual model is ≤1 per 6s. Driver: trigger {teamAmmo, count:100} + resourceGate min:13, i.e. ~1 check/s at the fixture's team fire rate. Driver documents it ('a ⚑ over-fire vs strict per-capture; the FIRST nuke at t~78 is correct, the count is cadence-dependent'). Board impact in the shipped control comp is exactly zero (the pool peaks ~7, so the block fires 0×), and the driver's H5 asserts that zero explicitly; the inflation shows up only in the disableBursts reachability run and would surface in any comp where accrual outruns the spend.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Faithful representation: attach the nuke to the CAPTURE event itself — a second interval:6 block, resourceGate ghost min:13, target enemy, ordered after the accrual block — so exactly one nuke fires per capture at cap. The driver's stated blocker is that a second `interval` block perturbs the team-generator beam-search invariant (scripts/tests/generators/burst-cooldown-coverage.ts topTeams(5)) at byte-identical damage; that is a HARNESS artifact, not a kit fact, so the correct resolution is to fix the generator's sensitivity to block structure and then re-cadence this block — not to leave the kit mis-cadenced. Until then the current form is acceptable only because it is provably board-inert in the shipped context.

gotchas.summary: The nuke's min:13 gate reads the pool AFTER the capture that reaches the cap, so the 12→13 capture can itself fire a proc the wording ('captured WHILE AT maximum capacity') does not grant.
gotchas.evidence: Kit S2 line 2 vs driver resourceGate {name:'ghost', min:13} on a pool-check that runs after the interval:6 accrual has already incremented. Independently flagged by the S6 blind in its own caveats ('the capture that takes 12→13 will therefore fire one 1100% proc… a one-per-battle over-credit') — a genuine cross-family convergence on the same off-by-one. Zero board impact in the shipped context (the pool never reaches 13 while bursting) and subsumed by the cadence issue above wherever it is reachable.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Fire the nuke on the capture-absorbed-by-the-cap signal — i.e. evaluate the gate on the PRE-add pool (min:13 read before the +1), so only a capture attempted while already at 13 procs it. Needs either a pre-add gate read or an explicit 'capture overflowed' event in the resource primitive; not fixable by changing the value.

gotchas.summary: 'Maintains at least 1 ghost' is dropped: a −6 spend from a pool of exactly 6 leaves 0, so the ≥1 caster-ATK aura lapses where the kit would keep it alive.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Number of ghosts ▼ 6. Maintains at least 1 ghost.' Driver: resource {min:0} + delta −6, with the line declared verbatim in `unmodeled.burst` and the reason given (min:1 would clamp `initial` to 1 and wrongly light the ≥1 tier at frame 0). The S6 blind independently unmodeled the same line for the same reason. Reachable in the shipped rotation — the pool sits ~6–7 at cast — so a cast at exactly 6 costs the whole Water team the 16.2% caster-ATK aura for ~6s plus the pool-check lag.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add a per-effect spend floor to the resource primitive (e.g. `resource {delta:-6, floor:1}`) so the spend clamps without moving the pool's initial value. Do NOT emulate it by raising the resource `min` — that breaks the frame-0 inertness the ≥1 tier depends on.

gotchas.summary: Rider crit is left unset on the burst hits and the nuke while the S6 blind authored crit:true — an unresolved divergence on ~4800% per cast plus the 1100% nuke.
gotchas.evidence: Driver ships flatDamage with no `crit` field and records the doubt in its own caveats ('SSOT says function-type damage crits at the caster's rate by default — verify/align repo-wide before changing'). S6 set crit:true on all 20 riders. SSOT damage-calculation.md §2b: function-type skill damage 'CRIT at the caster's rate (default on)', and §2d/§1b describe the stored-hit path as carrying the documented crit-OFF EXEMPTION that `storedHit.crit` removes — which reads as evidence that the ordinary flatDamage path already defaults crit-ON, in which case unset ≡ the blind's crit:true and the divergence is cosmetic.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Verify the flatDamage default in dealDamage directly (one grep, not a measurement). If it is crit-ON, nothing changes and the caveat should be closed with the citation; if it is crit-OFF, that is a repo-wide SSOT violation on every function-type rider and must be fixed at the engine default, NOT by adding crit:true to this one unit.

verdictRationale: GO — 13/13 kit lines land FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP, with no SILENT_DROP anywhere (every unmodeled sub-line, including 'Maintains at least 1 ghost' and the possession flavor, is declared verbatim) and no undocumented divergence, so there are no blocking gotchas. Ranked real findings, all documented and none GO-blocking: (1) the ≥4 Elemental-Advantage aura's polled 6s duration lets it linger up to ~6s past the burst spend that should close its gate, and that stale window sits inside Full Burst — the S6 blind hit the same engine wall and chose a ≤2s window, so a shorter duration on the teamAmmo blocks is available today without touching the generator issue; (2) the at-cap nuke fires per pool-check rather than per capture (~6× over-fire wherever reachable, provably zero board impact in the shipped comp); (3) the 12→13 post-add off-by-one, which the S6 blind found independently; (4) the inexpressible min-1 ghost floor; (5) the unresolved rider-crit default. Blind convergence is strong and mechanical: 22 of 23 executed S5 assertions are GREEN against the shipped override, and S6 independently reproduced the pool bounds, both threshold gates and their stats, the burstCast 40%, the discrete-800 sequential branches with the max-12/min-13 gates and the −6/−9 spends, and the block-ordering requirement — the sole RED is the S5 nuke-reachability assertion, which is a RECON_ERROR (it encodes the S5 author's own ⚑ premise that accrual outruns the spend and contradicts the S2b spec's explicit demand for the two-sided treatment the driver implemented via the engineered pool=13 and never-burst runs). Discrimination holds on every load-bearing claim — the unscoped-allies, ungated-nuke, engineered-13, disableBursts and Iron-boss counterfactuals each fail under their named nearest-wrong model — with one weakness to record: H1's 'first apply ≥1s' assertion does not by itself discriminate the ≥1 resourceGate (an ungated teamAmmo block would also first apply at ≈t1); the gate is caught only by H4's ≥20s assertion, so H4 must not be weakened. THE SAME-MODEL RESIDUAL THE OWNER MUST SPOT-CHECK IS ⚑1, THE ACCRUAL CADENCE: every agent here is one model, so the fact that S2b, S5 and S6 all independently leaned toward the 100-team-hit (teamAmmo) reading while the driver shipped the 6s cap is the single most informative disagreement in the packet — it decides whether the burst is normally 6 hits or 13, whether the 1100% nuke ever fires at all, and roughly a 1.7× swing in her board damage. The driver's textual argument ('Recurring interval: 6 sec' printed as part of the capture ability) is legitimate but genuinely ambiguous, and its supporting appeal to 'realistic board damage ~209M' is board-fit reasoning that carries no evidential weight — resolve it from footage by reading the ghost-counter UI delta (time-to-4 and time-to-13 in a never-burst context; ≈24s / ≈78s confirms the cap binds, near-immediate refutes it), and treat every magnitude downstream of this unit as provisional until that read lands.
